items.title: WHO chief arrives in Spain ahead of hantavirus ship docking

featured_image.name: WHO chief arrives in Spain before hantavirus-hit ship evacuation

items.description:
The MV Hondius, a Dutch-flagged expedition cruise ship at the center of a hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people, is expected to arrive in Tenerife in Spain's Canary Islands early Sunday morning, as WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus traveled to Spain on Saturday to personally oversee the disembarkation of more than 140 passengers and crew.[1][2][3]

"This is not another Covid," Tedros told residents of Tenerife, emphasizing that no one aboard the ship is currently showing symptoms and that "the risk for the population of Canary Islands and globally remains low."[4][3]

items.title: US restates opposition to West Bank annexation at UN

featured_image.name: US opposes Israeli annexation of West Bank, diplomat tells UN

items.description:
A U.S. diplomat told the United Nations on Friday that Washington opposes Israeli annexation of the occupied West Bank, restating a position the Trump administration has maintained since taking office amid growing alarm over settlement expansion and escalating violence against Palestinians.

Ambassador Jeff Bartos, the U.S. representative for U.N. Management and Reform, delivered the message during an Arria-formula session convened by the Security Council's five European members — Denmark, France, Greece, Latvia, and the United Kingdom — to hear testimony on conditions facing Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.[1][2]

"As President Trump has made clear, the United States opposes Israeli annexation of the West Bank," Bartos said. "Stability in the West Bank is vital for Israel's security and aligns with our goal of achieving peace in the region."[1]

items.title: US sanctions Chinese satellite firms over Iran war

featured_image.name: How Chinese satellites have boosted Iran's war effort

items.description: The United States on Friday imposed sanctions on three Chinese companies accused of supplying satellite imagery that enabled Iranian military strikes against American forces in the Middle East, a move that adds a layer of tension just days before President Donald Trump is set to visit Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

items.title: Israel to release two Gaza flotilla activists for deportation

featured_image.name: UN demands Israel release Gaza flotilla activists, investigate abuse claims

items.description: Two activists detained after Israeli forces intercepted the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla last month are being released from Israeli security detention on Saturday and will be deported in the coming days, according to their legal representatives and the human rights organization Adalah.[1][2]

items.title: Bahrain arrests 41 over alleged links to Iran's IRGC

featured_image.name: Bahrain Says it Has Arrested 41 People Linked to IRGC

items.description: Bahrain's Interior Ministry announced on Saturday the arrest of 41 individuals it described as members of a network linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, escalating a security crackdown that human rights groups say has disproportionately targeted the country's Shia Muslim population since the outbreak of war in the region.

items.title: US intel says Iran's Khamenei shaping war strategy

featured_image.name: What to know about Ali Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader

items.description: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is playing a key role in shaping Tehran's war strategy and negotiations with the United States despite remaining out of public view for more than two months, according to a U.S. intelligence assessment reported by CNN on Thursday. The assessment comes as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian confirmed he recently met with Khamenei in person, easing weeks of speculation about whether the wounded leader was capable of governing.[1]

items.title: Trump announces three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire with prisoner swap

featured_image.name: Trump announces 3-day ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine war

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, declaring on Truth Social that the pause will include a suspension of all kinetic activity and a prisoner exchange of 1,000 individuals from each country. The announcement came as both sides were already trading accusations of violating earlier, competing unilateral truces declared in the lead-up to Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio calls Iran's claim over Strait of Hormuz 'unacceptable' as U.S. awaits deal response

featured_image.name: Impostor uses AI to impersonate Rubio and contact foreign and U.S.  officials : NPR

items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared on Friday that Iran's effort to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz was "unacceptable," warning from Rome that the international community must be prepared to respond with "more than strongly worded statements" to push back against Tehran's claims over the critical waterway.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran's FM says missile arsenal grew despite US strikes

featured_image.name: Iran's Missile Arsenal in the 2026 Conflict

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Friday dismissed a U.S. intelligence assessment that Iran's missile capabilities had been degraded by months of American and Israeli strikes, claiming Tehran's arsenal has actually grown since the war began and declaring Iran "1,000% ready" to defend itself.

items.title: Satellite images reveal massive oil spill near Iran's Kharg Island

featured_image.name: Massive oil slicks spotted off Iran's Kharg Island as Trump touts Hormuz  clash

items.description: Satellite imagery has revealed a large oil spill spreading across dozens of square kilometers of sea near Iran's Kharg Island, the country's primary crude export terminal, as the U.S. naval blockade continues to choke Tehran's oil trade and push its storage capacity toward its limits.

items.title: US fires on two more Iranian tankers breaching blockade

featured_image.name: Tankers showing caution around Strait of Hormuz after attack on Iran

items.description:
The US military fired on and disabled two Iranian-flagged oil tankers on Friday that were attempting to violate the ongoing American naval blockade of Iran's ports, escalating tensions even as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a proposed deal to end the two-month war.

The strikes came two days after US forces disabled a third tanker, the M/T Hasna, on Wednesday by firing 20mm cannon rounds from an F/A-18 Super Hornet to knock out the vessel's rudder as it ignored warnings to stop in the Gulf of Oman, according to US Central Command.[1][2]

items.title: Trump-Xi summit proceeds despite Iran ceasefire strains

featured_image.name: Trump will travel to Beijing for rescheduled China trip May ...

items.description: President Donald Trump is pressing ahead with plans to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing next week, even as a fragile ceasefire with Iran threatens to unravel and Chinese officials harbor reservations about the timing of the high-stakes encounter.

items.title: Taiwan passes $25B defense bill for US arms purchases

featured_image.name: Taiwan legislature passes $25B defense bill for major US arms purchases

items.description: Taiwan's legislature on Friday passed a NT$780 billion ($24.8 billion) special defense spending bill to fund purchases of American weapons, ending months of partisan gridlock over the island's military preparedness against China — but delivering far less than President Lai Ching-te's government had sought.

items.title: Reform UK surges as Labour loses hundreds of seats in local elections

featured_image.name: Local election results live: Reform delivers blow to Labour but Starmer vows to stay

items.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed he would "not walk away" on Friday as early results from England's local elections revealed a punishing night for the Labour Party, with Nigel Farage's Reform UK making dramatic gains across the country's traditional Labour heartlands.

items.title: Iran warns UAE will 'pay the price' after Qeshm blasts

featured_image.name: CENTCOM carries out strikes on Iranian military facilities

items.description: Explosions rocked Iran's Qeshm Island and the port city of Bandar Abbas on Thursday night, prompting Iranian state-affiliated media to accuse the United Arab Emirates of carrying out a hostile action and warn that Abu Dhabi would face consequences if its involvement is confirmed.

items.title: Kremlin drafts plan to sell peace deal as victory, leaked documents show

featured_image.name: Kremlin - Moscow, Russia

items.description: Internal documents from Russia's Presidential Administration reveal the Kremlin has been developing a propaganda strategy since late winter 2026 to frame a potential negotiated end to the war in Ukraine as a Russian victory, according to an investigation published by the Dossier Center this week.

items.title: Venice Biennale hit by mass protests, historic strike planned for Friday

featured_image.name: In Venice, the World's Biggest Art Show Descends Into Infighting - WSJ

items.description: The 61st Venice Biennale has plunged into political crisis during its opening week, with mass protests, a jury walkout, and a funding cut by the European Union transforming the world's most prestigious art exhibition into a battleground over the participation of Russia and Israel.

items.title: US strikes Iran after warships attacked in Hormuz

featured_image.name: Centcom denies claim US warship hit by Iranian missiles

items.description: The United States and Iran exchanged fire on Thursday as three U.S. Navy destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz, marking the most serious escalation since the two countries agreed to a ceasefire on April 8. U.S. Central Command said it intercepted the Iranian attacks and struck back at military facilities inside Iran, while President Trump dismissed the retaliatory strikes as a "love tap" and insisted the ceasefire remained intact.

items.title: Trump gives EU until July 4 to ratify trade deal

featured_image.name: Von der Leyen calls Trump in new u-turn on tariffs

items.description: President Donald Trump on Thursday issued a new ultimatum to the European Union, giving the bloc until July 4 — the 250th anniversary of American independence — to ratify a trade framework agreed last summer or face escalated tariffs. The announcement came after a phone call with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and hours after EU negotiators failed to reach a breakthrough in overnight talks on the deal's implementing legislation.

items.title: Iran reviews US peace memo as Trump threatens bombing

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Iran with bombs unless nuclear deal reached

items.description:
Iran said on Wednesday it is still reviewing a US peace proposal that could bring the war to an end, even as President Donald Trump renewed threats of military action against the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached.

An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson told the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) that "the American proposal is still under examination by Iran, and once it is finalized, it will convey its opinion to the Pakistani side," referring to Pakistan's role as mediator in the negotiations.[1][2]

Trump, speaking from the Oval Office, struck an optimistic tone: "They want to make a deal. We've had very good talks over the last 24 hours, and it's very possible that we'll make a deal". But hours later, he issued a stark warning on Truth Social: "If they don't agree, the bombing starts, and it will be, sadly, at a much higher level and intensity than it was before".[3][2][4]
